In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

Lalitadevi said to the boy, “Will you step with me into the garden?”
options_en: Lalitadevi asked the boy if he would step with her into the garden.
Lalitadevi said to the boy if he would step with me in the garden.
Lalitadevi said to the boy if he would like to step with me in the garden.
Lalitadevi requested the boy to step with me in the garden.
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, said in Direct Speech is changed into enquired (of), wanted to know, asked, etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in the Direct Speech whose answer can come as Yes or No in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions if or whether.

For example:

Ravi said to me, Is she studying? (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

said to’ into ‘asked’" "you' becomes "he", 'will' becomes 'would'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

King Krishnadevaraya loved horses and had a collection of some of the best breeds of horses in his stable. Once a horse trader from Arabia came to the court of Krishnadevaraya and told him that he had some very good breed of Arabian horses for sale. The King loved the horse and told him that he would like all his horses. The King paid him 5000 gold coins as an advance, and the trader promised that he would return with the other horses in 2 days before leaving.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

The search has been _____ (impeded) by a lack of fuel for a rescue helicopter.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate synonym for the word 'impeded' is 'hampered'. "Impeded" means to delay or slow down the progress of something by obstructing or hindering it. "Hampered" also means to restrict the movement or progress of something, typically by creating obstacles or limitations. In the sentence, both words convey the idea that the search has been slowed down or obstructed by the lack of fuel for the rescue helicopter. "Advanced" means to move forward or make progress. "Promoted" means to further the progress, growth, or development of something. "Restored" means to bring back something to its original or former condition. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The search has been hampered by a lack of fuel for a rescue helicopter.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

The manager said to me, "I'm going to call you right now."
options_en: The manager told me that he is going to call me right then.
The manager told me that he was going to call me right then.
The manager told me that he was going to call him right now.
The manager told me that he would call me right then.
questions.solution_en:
Option (b) is the correct answer.

The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Continuous Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + ing + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject + V2 + ing + Object).

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

• The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

• Inverted commas are removed and 'that' is added before the statement.

• The pronouns 'I' and 'you' are changed into 'he' and 'me' respectively.

• The helping verb 'am' is changed into 'was'.

• 'Right now' is changed into 'right then'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The manager told me that he was going to call me right then.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I managed to ____ a quiet cafe to enjoy a moment of solitude.
questions.solution_en:
The correct option to fill in the blank is (d) "find." In the sentence "I managed to find a quiet cafe to enjoy a moment of solitude," the phrase "to find" functions as an infinitive. An infinitive is the base form of a verb preceded by the word "to." It is commonly used after certain verbs, such as "manage," to express purpose, intention, or the completion of an action.

In this context, "to find" indicates the purpose or goal of the action - finding a quiet cafe for a moment of solitude. The use of the base form "find" after "to" in the infinitive structure is appropriate for expressing the intended outcome of the speaker's effort to manage a moment of solitude. 'Find' aligns with the use of the infinitive structure in English grammar, conveying the purpose or goal associated with the action of managing a moment of solitude. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The final sentence: I managed to find a quiet café to enjoy a moment of solitude.
